title: Annotate embedded code strings for editor tooling
goal: Mark string parameters as C#, F# or Visual Basic source so supporting editors can recognise the embedded language without implying runtime validation or execution.

selectionNotes: Annotations are metadata only. Editor assistance depends on that editor and language service; no particular editor support or UI behavior is verified.
Invalid source still passes through these sample methods unchanged; parsing, compilation and execution require separate application logic.

runtime.name: .NET
runtime.reason: The newer framework APIs and caller behavior are .NET 11 contracts.

sdk.name: .NET SDK
sdk.reason: Build against .NET 11 reference assemblies; exact RC2 artifacts are test baselines.

language.name: C#
language.reason: Declared canonical sample language mode; these APIs need no preview language syntax.

platforms: Any platform supported by .NET 11; managed checks executed on Windows x64.
prerequisites: SDK console project with TargetFramework=net11.0, LangVersion=15.0, ImplicitUsings=enable and Nullable=enable. Put declarations in namespace Playbook.Samples.
constraints: Annotations are metadata only. Editor assistance depends on that editor and language service; no particular editor support or UI behavior is verified.
Invalid source still passes through these sample methods unchanged; parsing, compilation and execution require separate application logic.
No query provider, rendering integration, external account, resource provisioning or optional workload is required. No unverified older-target route is advertised.
stabilityLimitations: Verified with .NET 11 RC2; GA reconciliation remains pending. These selected APIs have no publisher experimental annotation or required experimental opt-in.

evidence.scope: Real compilation/execution checks C#/F#/Visual Basic attribute identifiers, unchanged invalid source, five exact video media types, data versus HTTPS addresses and rejected relative/unknown-format inputs. No editor UI, payload parsing or media playback is claimed.
